test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Motor Vehicle) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following types of seats is made of hardened alloys and pressed or shrunk into the cylinder head, often used in aluminium engines for better durability?
solution:
The correct answer is __Insert valve seats**(Option 4)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Insert valve seats__ are designed for durability and precision in engine operation.
 
• These seats are made of hardened alloys to withstand high temperatures and wear.
 
• They are either pressed or shrunk into the cylinder head for a secure fit.
 
• Insert valve seats are commonly used in aluminium engines to enhance performance and longevity.
 
• They provide improved resistance to deformation and cracking under stress.
 
• This design ensures optimal sealing between the valve and the cylinder head, ensuring efficient engine operation.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ring valve seats:**
 
 
• These are typically integrated into the cylinder head and not as commonly used as insert valve seats in modern engines.
 
 
 
• **Butterfly valve seats:**
 
 
• Primarily used in butterfly valves to regulate fluid flow, not suitable for engine applications.
 
 
 
• **Integral valve seats:**
 
 
• These are machined directly into the cylinder head material, offering limited durability compared to insert valve seats.
